subject: [Kernel] Fix SM90 FP8 decode regression with benchmarked M/K/N routing (#37018)
pr_body:
## Motivation

The SM90 row/column-scaled FP8 selector introduced by #34318 can route decode GEMMs to `torch._scaled_mm` based on K/N alone. The [reported H100 W8A8 regression](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34318#issuecomment-5461656173) is:

- model: `Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-FP8-dynamic`
- test: `test/registered/quant/test_w8a8_quantization.py::TestW8A8Fp8.test_throughput`
- batch size: 1
- throughput: approximately 215 tok/s before #34318, approximately 190 tok/s after it
- affected down projection: `M=1, K=14336, N=4096`

Direct profiling of that shape on both H200 and H100 showed that the AOT kernel is substantially faster at decode M, even though K and N are large.

## Modifications

Constrain Torch/NVJet routing to the benchmarked large-prefill envelope (doing m >= 6144 is not really worth the gain from my measurements):

```python
m >= 8192 and (
    (k >= 4096 and n >= 6144) or
    (k >= 7168 and n >= 5376)
)
```

This keeps the following on AOT:

- all decode and small-prefill calls with `M < 8192`
- the reported `K=14336, N=4096` Llama down projection
- narrow TP8 projections `K=5376, N=3584` and `K=3584, N=5376`
- shapes outside the measured projection envelope

Torch remains selected for stable large-prefill wins: wide QKV/gate/up projections and broad down projections.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Common software:

- PyTorch 2.11.0+cu130 (`70d99e998b4955e0049d13a98d77ae1b14db1f45`)
- CUDA 13.0
- `sgl_kernel==0.4.4`
- CUDA-event timing with randomized/interleaved AOT and Torch samples

The broad grid used 11 projection families and 12 M values (132 cases): 1, 16, 64, 256, 1024, 2048, 4096, 6144, 8192, 8320, 12288, and 16384. Percentages below are Torch speedups over AOT.

### H200 (SM90)

Protocol:

- broad grid: 5 warmups and 15 samples per arm
- two randomized boundary confirmations: 44 cases and 33 cases, with 8–10 warmups and 30–40 samples per arm
- exact-workload conditioning before timing

Reported regression shape:

| M | K | N | AOT | Torch | Result |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 1 | 14336 | 4096 | 26.50 µs | 51.12 µs | AOT is 1.93× faster |

Routing boundary:

| K |  …[truncated]

subject: [Bugfix] Fix MLA kv_b_proj activation dtype with Marlin FP8 (#38771)
pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes #38658.

This PR fixes an MLA prefill dtype bug when FP8 weights are served through the Marlin path on GPUs without native FP8 support (`sm < 89`).

On affected GPUs, Marlin repacks FP8 weights into `torch.int32`. In `vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/mla_attention.py`, `_compute_prefill_context()` was using `self.kv_b_proj.weight.dtype` to determine how to cast `kv_c_normed` before passing it to `kv_b_proj`.

After Marlin repacking, that dtype becomes `torch.int32`, which reflects the packed storage format rather than the expected activation compute dtype. This can cause MLA to cast activations to `int32`, and the Marlin kernel then fails with: `RuntimeError: unsupported 'a' scalar_type`

This change switches MLA to use `self.kv_b_proj.params_dtype`, which correctly tracks the layer's compute/input dtype even when the stored weight tensor has been repacked.

This PR also adds a focused regression test covering the dtype selection logic in `_compute_prefill_context()`.

## Test Plan

### Targeted regression and unit coverage

```
python -m pytest tests/model_executor/layers/attention/test_mla_attention.py -v
```

### Local reproduction

Reproduced the root cause locally on an affected GPU (`sm_86`) and confirmed that using the repacked `torch.int32` storage dtype for activation casting triggers `RuntimeError: unsupported 'a' scalar_type`

## Test Result

### Hardware used for local reproduction

- AWS EC2 `g5.xlarge`
- GPU: NVIDIA A10G
- CUDA capability: `sm_86`

### Targeted regression test
```
tests/model_executor/layers/attention/test_mla_attention.py::test_compute_prefill_context_uses_kv_b_proj_params_dtype PASSED
```

### Local validation before fix

Verified the failure mechanism described in the issue:

- Marlin repacks FP8 weights to `torch.int32`
- the old MLA logic selected `weight.dtype`
- activations were cast to `int32`
- Marlin failed with: `RuntimeError: unsupported 'a' scalar_type`

subject: [DSA] Fix the pooled-indexer breakable prefill bridge under DP attention (#41311)
pr_body:
## Summary

Fixes a crash with `--enable-dp-attention` + `--cuda-graph-backend-prefill breakable` on GLM-5.3-Flash:

```
ValueError: Pooled-indexer prefill returned an unexpected top-k shape
```

- DP pads `extend_num_tokens` (52) past the logical tokens (9); the indexer returns only the 9 logical rows.
- Bridge now requires `logical <= rows <= padded`, copies the logical rows and fills the rest with `-1` (like eager `_pad_topk_indices`).

Tested on 4x GB300 (TP4, DP2 and DP4, concurrent uneven prompts): crash before, pass after.

subject: [Bugfix] Handle Asym W4A16 (ConchLinearKernel) for CT (#33200)
pr_body:
Fix ConchLinearKernel to correctly handle asymmetric quantization (uint4/uint8 with explicit zero points) on ROCm.

## Purpose

Root cause: The Conch kernel expects unpacked zero points with shape (K//G, N), but vLLM was passing packed zeros with shape (N//pack, K//G). This caused out-of-bounds memory access resulting in: `HIP error: an illegal memory access was encountered`

The fix unpacks the zero points from packed int32 format and reorders them to match the kernel's expected layout. The unpacking logic now correctly handles both 4-bit (8 values/int32) and 8-bit (4 values/int32) quantization based on the weight type's bit width.

## Test Plan
```
vllm bench latency --model RedHatAI/Qwen3-8B-quantized.w4a16 --num-iters 1
```

## Test Result
Crashes before this PR, succeeds with this PR.

Compared outputs with Qwen/Qwen3-8B-AWQ (same base model, AWQ quantization). Both models produce identical correct answers on 8 test questions (100% match).

Note: No unit test added - we could not find a small asymmetric CT W4A16 model. 
Note: The fix also handles asymmetric uint8, but we could not find such a model on HuggingFace to validate (all W8A16 CT models found are symmetric).

subject: [Fix][ROCm] MXFP4 MoE round-up inflates TP-sharded expert weights on CDNA3, starving KV cache (#56359)
pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes #53961

While testing #53961, I found that the per-GPU VRAM used for weight loading is 135.35 GiB (without EP) vs 103.54 GiB (with EP). Upon closer investigation, it is caused by the rocm's branch of `mxfp4_round_up_hidden_size_and_intermediate_size` which rounds the intermediate moe size to 256 which inflated the expert weights usage. Before this PR, an existing special case for Kimi-K3 (AITER+SiLU/SiTU) already aligns to 128 instead of 256.

Concretely, for DeepSeek-V4-Pro (`moe_intermediate_size=3072`, TP=8, no EP):
- per-partition intermediate = 3072/8 = **384** fp4 elems (192 B)
- round_up(384, 256) = **512** → `w13_weight` created as `(384, 1024, 3584)` instead of `(384, 768, 3584)` → **+33% expert weights = +30 GiB/GPU**
- with the default `max_num_batched_tokens` (16384 since #51726), caused the observation from #53961 

EP wasn't affected because each GPU holds whole experts, so the intermediate dimension stays at its native 3072 (already aligned); without EP, TP slices it to 384 per GPU, which is not aligned and gets padded.

## Change

I extended the existing 128-alignment exception to also cover TRITON_UNFUSED with SiLU/SiTU activation. The pre-existing AITER arm is unchanged: K3's AITER kernel (gfx950-only) handles its native intermediate size (moe_intermediate 3072; e.g. 384/partition at TP8), so K3 keeps 128 on CDNA4.

For the new TRITON_UNFUSED arm, the 128-alignment is gated to CDNA != 4, because opt_flags_amd sets matmul_ogs's block_k=128 whenever weight scales are present on CDNA != 4 (always the case for mxfp4 W4A16 checkpoints) — the unpadded 384-element shard already satisfies the kernel's even-K requirement.  gpt-oss (SWIGLUOAI, tuned in #38043) keeps 256.

In essence, the checks keeps the pre-existing Kimi-K3, gpt-oss handling while letting DeepSeek-V4 Pro (TRITON_UNFUSED + SiLU/SiTU on CDNA3) keeps the 128 size without rounding up to 256. 

## Test Plan

Tested the before/after using this serve command:

```
# max batched tokens: 16384 will failed before this PR
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --block-siz …[truncated]

subject: fix: KT's last MoE layer stops deferring experts again (#36921)
pr_body:
## Motivation

`create_kt_config_from_server_args` resolves `num_layers` for one reason: so the
KT wrapper can recognise the model's final layer, which must defer no experts.

```python
if (self.kt_config.max_deferred_experts_per_token is not None
        and self.kt_config.num_layers is not None
        and self.kt_config.layer_idx == self.kt_config.num_layers - 1):
    layer_max_deferred = 0
```

That branch has not fired since December 2025.

#12834 wrote the read as `server_args.get_hf_config()`, which was correct at the
time. #15298 removed `ServerArgs.get_hf_config` and rewrote the three call sites
*inside* `server_args.py` to `get_model_config().hf_config` — but not this one,
which lives in another file. The call has raised `AttributeError` on every
invocation since.

Three things kept it quiet:

- the read sat inside a bare `except Exception: pass` whose comment described the
  intended case (*"If we can't get the config, num_layers will be None"*), so the
  failure was indistinguishable from the handled one;
- the consumer guards on `num_layers is not None`, so the symptom is a rule that
  silently stops applying, not an error;
- the function returns early unless `kt_weight_path` is set, so only
  KTransformers runs reach it at all.

## Modifications

The read becomes `server_args.get_model_config().hf_config` — the same spelling
#15298 moved everything else to — and the swallow is gone. Three lines in, eight
out.

## Accuracy Tests

Measured on an 8×H200 box against a 7-layer checkpoint:

| | `KTConfig.num_layers` | layer 6 recognised as last |
|---|---|---|
| main | `None` | no |
| this PR | `7` | yes |

`sa.get_hf_config()` on main raises `AttributeError: 'ServerArgs' object has no
attribute 'get_hf_config'`, confirming the call could never have succeeded.
`test/registered/unit/layers/moe/` is green (54 passed).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

None. One attribute read replaces one that always raised.

subject: [diffusion] fix: run an all-valid attention mask on the backend's unmasked kernel (#41309)
pr_body:
## Problem

On sm100 the default attention backend resolves to `DYNAMIC_CUDNN_SDPA`, but `USPAttention`'s masked local path opens its varlen fast path only for `backend == FA`. Every other backend gets a dense additive mask for `torch.nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention`, and any mask moves SDPA off flash and cuDNN onto PyTorch's `fmha_cutlassF_*_sm80` kernel, even when the mask masks nothing.

Ideogram4 passes such a mask on both guidance branches at batch 1: its text is never padded at batch 1, so `segment_ids > 0` is all true. Every attention call on B200 therefore took the cutlassF path:

- torch profile of the denoising loop: attention = **54% of GPU time on 1×B200, 47% at TP2**, all in `fmha_cutlassF_bf16_aligned_32x128_gmem_sm80`
- per call (`[1, 18, 4126, 256]` bf16): **2.19 ms with the mask, 0.81 ms without**

It is also consistent with Ideogram4 measuring only ~9% faster on B200 than on H200, against 1.7-2.6× for the other models: on Hopper the default backend is FA, whose varlen path already treats an all-valid mask as dense.

## Fix

When `attn_mask_meta` shows every key valid (its index count equals the mask's element count, known on the host, no device sync), the masked local path runs the backend's own unmasked kernel. Segmented-prefix inputs (Qwen-Image) are concatenated first, so the prefix is kept. Masks with real padding, and meta without indices (padding-gap meta), keep the masked path. The FA backend is untouched (its varlen branch returns before this point), and so are the sequence-parallel paths.

## Validation (4×B200)

- Unit: the new `test/unit/test_usp_all_valid_key_mask.py` drives `USPAttention.forward` through the masked local branch with real varlen meta. An all-valid mask runs the backend kernel once and matches unmasked attention; a real padding mask, and padding-gap meta without indices, keep the masked path; a segmented prefix is concatenated before dispatch. The two backend-kernel tests fail on `main`. The neighbouring attention/mask unit tests (ring tail-pad, K/V gather, varlen meta, replicated prefix, Ideogram4, BCG padding) pass.

- Ideogram4 serving, default B200 command (`--tp-size 2`), warmup then 5 measured reques …[truncated]

subject: [LoRA] Fix EP + per-expert MoE LoRA illegal memory access (#23178)
pr_body:
## Summary

Two related bugs prevent `--tp N --ep M --enable-lora --lora-backend triton --moe-runner-backend triton` from running on any MoE model with per-expert LoRA adapters; both reliably crash in the first forward pass with `CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered`. This PR fixes both and adds unit coverage.

### Bug 1 — `LoRAMemoryPool` sizes per-expert buffers for the global expert count

`FusedMoEWithLoRA` allocates LoRA A/B buffers via `LoRAMemoryPool`, whose per-expert shape was `[num_loras, num_global_experts, ...]`. Under EP, however, `StandardDispatcher` remaps `topk_ids` from global → local IDs *before* the MoE kernel (see `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/token_dispatcher/standard.py`), so both the base MoE weights and the LoRA delta kernels are indexed with IDs in `[0, num_local_experts)` plus a `-1` sentinel. A LoRA buffer sized `[..., 128, ...]` being indexed with local IDs `[0, 32)` therefore reads the wrong expert's weights (or, combined with bug #2, triggers the illegal access).

### Bug 2 — `moe_lora_align_block_size` doesn't filter the `-1` sentinel in one branch

`_count_and_sort_expert_tokens` only rejected `expert_id >= num_experts`:

```cpp
for (size_t i = tid; i < numel; i += stride) {
  int32_t expert_id = topk_ids[i];
  if (expert_id >= num_experts) { continue; }      // <-- no `< 0`
  ...
  int32_t rank_post_pad = atomicAdd(
    &cumsum_buffer[(model_offset * (num_experts + 1)) + expert_id], 1);
  sorted_token_ids[max_num_tokens_padded * model_offset + rank_post_pad] = i;
}
```

`-1` passes that guard and produces:
- `atomicAdd(&cumsum_buffer[model_offset * (num_experts+1) + (-1)], 1)` — OOB write (negative stride), and
- `sorted_token_ids[offset + rank_post_pad]` with a garbage `rank_post_pad`.

Both sibling call sites in the same file already guard `expert_id < 0 || expert_id >= num_experts`. This PR makes the third call site consistent.

- **`python/sglang/srt/lora/mem_pool.py`**
  - Capture `(moe_ep_size, moe_ep_rank)` and `moe_use_local_expert_ids` at pool init. The latter is `True` iff `moe_ep_size > 1` **and** the active runner remaps to local IDs (Triton/DeepGEMM/Marlin)  …[truncated]

subject: [Security] Fix info disclosure via int32 truncation in GGUF dequantize kernels (#44971)
pr_body:
## Purpose

Fix an information disclosure vulnerability caused by integer truncation in GGUF dequantize kernels (csrc/libtorch_stable/quantization/gguf/).

The to_cuda_ggml_t function pointer typedef declares its element count parameter k as int (32-bit). When a GGUF model has weight tensor dimensions whose product exceeds INT_MAX (e.g. a 65536x65536 matrix), the int64_t product m * n is silently truncated to int at the call site. The CUDA kernel then processes only the truncated number of elements. Since output tensors are allocated with torch::empty (uninitialized memory), the unfilled portion retains stale GPU memory which — in multi-tenant inference deployments — may contain tensor data from other users' requests.

Changes:

- Widen k from int to int64_t in the to_cuda_ggml_t typedef (ggml-common.h) and all 18 dequantize function signatures in dequantize.cuh
- Widen the dequantize_block kernel's index arithmetic to int64_t to match
- Widen col, batch, vecs, and padded local variables in gguf_kernel.cu from int to int64_t to prevent the same class of truncation in the matmul and MoE paths
- Defense-in-depth: zero-initialize all output tensors via torch::stable::fill_(Y, 0.0) in ggml_dequantize, ggml_mul_mat_vec_a8, ggml_mul_mat_a8, and ggml_moe_a8, so that even if a future truncation bug occurs, stale GPU memory is never exposed

## Test Plan

```
# Build and verify compilation succeeds
python setup.py build_ext --inplace
# Run existing GGUF tests to verify no regression
python -m pytest tests/ -k "gguf" -v
```

The type change from int to int64_t is ABI-compatible and all downstream call sites already pass int64_t values (e.g. m * n in ggml_dequantize). The fix eliminates the silent truncation at the function pointer boundary.

## Test Result

- All existing GGUF kernel call sites pass int64_t values — the widened signatures eliminate the implicit narrowing conversion
- clang-format passes on all changed files
- ggml_moe_a8_vec already used fill_(Y, 0.0) — the other four functions now match

subject: [ROCm][Bugfix] Use token-level KV indices in the aiter ASM context-prefill gather (#36852)
pr_body:
## Motivation

#36758 added an ASM fp8 varlen path for context-chunk prefill on gfx950, and at
the default `--page-size 1` it is a solid win: measured +4-10% end-to-end
throughput and a 5-9% TTFT reduction at 60k input on Qwen3.8-2.4T with TP8. This PR
extends it to `page_size > 1`, where we ran into accuracy issues due to an indexing mismatch.

The gather derives its pool slots like this:
`aiter_backend.py`:
```python
page_slot = kv_indptr[seq_ids].to(torch.long) + pos_in_seq // page
tok_idx = kv_pages[page_slot].to(torch.long) * page + pos_in_seq % page
```

That treats `kv_indptr` / `kv_indices` as page-granular. As far as I can tell they
are actually token-level at every page size, even when the allocator is
page-based: `AiterIndicesUpdaterPrefill` builds `kv_indptr = cumsum(seq_lens)` and
`create_flashinfer_kv_indices_triton` writes one `kv_indices` entry per token. So
token `t` of sequence `i` is already at pool slot `kv_indices[kv_indptr[i] + t]`,
with no page indirection to undo. There is a comment a few hundred lines up in the
same file that says:

```python
# Non-unified AITER CUDA graph paths fill this buffer with flat
# token-level kv_indices via create_flashinfer_kv_indices_triton
# (kv_indptr = cumsum(seq_lens)).  Even when the allocator is
# page-based, these writes are per-token, [...]
# TODO(aiter, page_size>1): root fix is to make page_size>1
# actually engage the attention kernel [...]
```

At `page_size=1` the two readings are the same expression (`t // 1 == t`,
`t % 1 == 0`, `slot * 1 == slot`), so the default path is exactly right and
nothing about the configuration #36758 benchmarked changes. Above 1 it goes one
of two ways depending on how full the KV pool is:

- the computed `tok_idx` leaves the pool, the second bounds check catches it, and
  we fall back to `ck_tile` - correct results, but the ASM path never engages;
- the computed `tok_idx` happens to stay inside the pool, both checks pass, and
  attention reads from the wrong slots.

## Modifications

Index the token table directly:
```python
kv_slot = kv_indptr[seq_ids] + pos_in_seq
tok_idx = kv_indices[kv_slot].to(torch.long)
```

subject: [Spec] Fix Gemma 4 MTP with `trtllm_mha` crash issue (#26966)
pr_body:
## Motivation

`trtllm_mha` + FROZEN_KV MTP (NEXTN) on hybrid-SWA models (e.g. Gemma-4) crashes with a CUDA illegal memory access once the SWA pool fills past the SWA-vs-full layer ratio (issue [#26957](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/26957), prior attempt [#26531](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/26531)). `TRTLLMHAAttnBackend` cached its SWA state at `__init__` from `model_runner.token_to_kv_pool`. On the draft worker that is the draft's own non-SWA pool, so `use_sliding_window_kv_pool` was `False` and the SWA→full page-index translation became dead code — SWA layers then got raw full-pool indices and read the smaller SWA k-cache out of bounds.

## Modifications

- Resolve the SWA pool from `model_runner.token_to_kv_pool_allocator` (`get_kvcache()`) instead of `token_to_kv_pool`. In FrozenKVMTP the draft's `token_to_kv_pool` is swapped to the target's `SWAKVPool` per forward call, but `token_to_kv_pool_allocator` is set once at init and is stable — the correct source of truth.
- Mirrors FlashInfer, which already gates SWA eligibility on the allocator (`isinstance(token_to_kv_pool_allocator, SWATokenToKVPoolAllocator)`, `flashinfer_backend.py:1027`).
- Not registering the Gemma-4 draft as hybrid-SWA: the draft owns no KV (frozen), so its own `SWAKVPool` would be keyed by draft layer ids while attention runs on remapped target layer ids (KeyError + wasted alloc); the allocator already points at the correct target pool.

## Accuracy Tests

Reproduced end-to-end on B200 (SM100) with [repro_26957_e2e.py](https://gist.github.com/kpham-sgl/d696a3b8c2fdc959c940f7a8afdd9c9b): crashes before the fix (CUDA illegal memory access), passes after.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

subject: [NVIDIA] Fix trtllm fp4 moe backend when used in MTP (#9384)
pr_body:
This PR addresses the issue mentioned [here](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/9238#issuecomment-3199279509).

The root cause is that some MoE layers may use an unquantized method. For example:
```
model.layers.3.mlp.experts → quantized  
model.decoder.mlp.experts  → unquantized
```

This may be triggered by the MTP settings.

`FusedMoE` works with both quantized and unquantized methods, which explains why the `flashinfer_cutlass` fp4 backend works fine.

`FlashInferFP4MoE` (i.e. the `flashinfer_trtllm` backend), however, only supports the modelopt_fp4 quantized method and fails with unquantized ones.

This PR fixes the issue by checking the quantization config. If no quantization config is found, we fall back to `FusedMoE`.

subject: [Bugfix] Fix RMSNorm kernels to multiply in weight's native dtype (#42379)
pr_body:
## Purpose

Fix a regression introduced by #40860 (DeepSeek V4 support) where `csrc/layernorm_kernels.cu` was changed to always upcast the RMSNorm weight to `float32` before the final multiplication. The correct behaviour, per the Python spec in `vllm/ir/ops/layernorm.py:20`, is to multiply in the weight's native dtype (BF16/FP16):

```python
x = x.to(weight.dtype) * weight  # multiply in weight.dtype
```

The FP32 weight path introduces ~0.03 per-element error per layer. For models with many Q/K RMSNorm layers (e.g. LLaDA-2, DeepSeek with Q/K norm) this compounds catastrophically — 20-layer cumulative divergence exceeds 100, and only ~2% of output tokens match the reference.

The bug was reproduced locally on an A100-SXM4-40GB before implementing the fix, confirming the reported max diff of ~3e-02. The fix was built from source and verified on the same hardware.

Fixes #42325

## Changes

**`csrc/layernorm_kernels.cu`** — 3 locations:
- `rms_norm_kernel` vectorized path
- `fused_add_rms_norm_kernel` FP16/BF16 optimised path
- `fused_add_rms_norm_kernel` generic scalar fallback

Pattern in each location:
```cpp
// Before (regressed in #40860):
float w = static_cast<float>(weight_elem);
out = static_cast<scalar_t>(x * s_variance * w);

// After (restores v0.19.1 behaviour):
out = static_cast<scalar_t>(x * s_variance) * weight_elem;
```

**`csrc/layernorm_quant_kernels.cu`** — 3 matching locations:
The FP8 quant kernels contain an explicit comment explaining they were designed to match the non-fused composite path (`rms_norm` output → `static_scaled_fp8_quant`). After fixing the non-fused path, the quant kernels require the same update to stay consistent. Without it, `test_fused_rms_norm_quant` fails because the two paths diverge.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/core/test_layernorm.py -x -q
pytest tests/kernels/ir/test_layernorm.py -x -q
```

Regression repro script (shows `FIXED` after patch):

```python
import torch
from vllm import _custom_ops as ops

x = torch.randn(48, 128, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device='cuda')
weight = torch.randn(128, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device='cuda')
out = torch.empty_like(x)
 …[truncated]

subject: [ROCm][AITER][Bugfix] Switch AITER to use PIECEWISE_AND_FULL compilation (#25104)
pr_body: ## Purpose AiterFlashAttentionBackend (enabled through VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MHA=1) does not work correctly with cudagraph_mode = FULL, since it calls two AITER kernels for prefill (aiter.flash_attn_varlen_func) and decode (aiter.paged_attention_v1). The correct AttentionCGSupport and cudagraph_mode to use here are `AttentionCGSupport.UNIFORM_SINGLE_TOKEN_DECODE` and `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` respectively. ## Test Plan For e.g. Llama 3.3 70B FP8 TP1 max_conc=256 on MI355, this fixes both OOMs as well as some accuracy issues we've been seeing. ## Test Result Serving command: ``` vllm serve amd/Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct-FP8-KV -tp 1 --max-num-batched-tokens 131072 --max-num-seqs 1024 --max-seq-len-to-capture 16384 --max-model-len 10240 --swap-space 64 --no-enable-prefix-caching --disable-log-requests --disable-uvicorn-access-log --trust-remote-code --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 -O '{"compilation_config":"FULL"}' ``` CG capture: LM-Eval: ``` lm_eval --model local-completions --model_args model=$MODEL,base_url=http://0.0.0.0:8000/v1/completions,num_concurrent=256,max_retries=10,max_gen_toks=2048 --batch_size auto --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --limit 250 --output_path . --apply_chat_template 2>&1 | tee -a eval.log INFO 09-17 22:05:58 [__init__.py:241] Automatically detected platform rocm. 2025-09-17:22:06:00 WARNING [__main__:369] --limit SHOULD ONLY BE USED FOR TESTING.REAL METRICS SHOULD NOT BE COMPUTED USING LIMIT. 2025-09-17:22:06:00 INFO [__main__:446] Selected Tasks: ['gsm8k'] 2025-09-17:22:06:00 INFO [evaluator:202] Setting random seed to 0 | Setting numpy seed to 1234 | Setting torch manual seed to 1234 | Setting fewshot manual seed to 1234 2025-09-17:22:06:00 INFO [evaluator:240] Initializing local-completions model, with arguments: {'model': 'amd/Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct-FP8-KV', 'base_url': 'http://0.0.0.0:8000/v1/completions', 'num_concurrent': 256, 'max_retries': 10, 'max_gen_toks': 2048} 2025-09-17:22:06:00 WARNING [models.api_models:158] Automatic batch size is not supported for API models.
